texts.preamble: Chandresh Pathak vs State Of U.P. on 14 December, 2023 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:237183 Court No. - 69 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 687 of 2016 Revisionist :- Chandresh Pathak Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- Krishna Kumar Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. (Order on Revision) 1.
texts.arguments: Subsequently, a notice under section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is said to be sent to the revisionist on 19.03.2009. It is further argued that the complaint in the present matter although is dated 04.03.2009 but the same has been filed on 20.03.2009 as would appear from the records on which the concerned trial court directed it to be registered on the said date. It is argued that there is delay in sending of the notice under section 13(2) of the Act inasmuch as section 13(2) of the Act prescribes the notice under it to be sent to the accused within 10 days of the receipt of the report of the Public Analyst but in the present case the report of the Public Analyst is dated 22.11.2008 which as per P.W.-2 Rajeev Kamal the food clerk and annexure ka-9 the postal receipt was sent to the revisionist on 19.03.2009 which is after about 4 months of the date of the report of the Public Analyst. It is further argued that even further there is no finding recorded by the trial court and even the appellate court that the said notice has been served upon the revisionist-accused. The service of notice is necessary for the accused-revisionist to exercise his option for getting the sample retested by the Central Food Laboratory. It is argued that even the trial court has not gone into the aspect by considering the records as to whether any evidence has been led by the prosecution regarding the service of notice under section 13(2) of the Act upon the revisionist. 5. Learned counsel for the revisionist has relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Vijendra Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763 (para-14 and 15) and Narayan Prasad Sahu Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87 (para-5, 6, 8 and 9) to buttress his argument. 6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the revision.
